"5명 중 4명은 아직 안 샀다"…아마존, K뷰티판 더 키운다 신규 판매자 50곳, 첫해 매출 100만달러 목표 선도 브랜드 7곳 집중 지원…신규 시장 개척도 신화숙 아마존 글로벌셀링 코리아 대표./사진=아마존 글로벌셀링 코리아 제공 아마존이 K뷰티 지원 전략의 무게중심을 신규 브랜드 발굴에서 매출 확대와 선도 브랜드 육성으로 옮긴다. K뷰티 열풍을 일시적 유행에 그치지 않고 지속 가능한 성장으로 이어가기 위해 신규 판매자의 시장 안착을 돕고, 성장 잠재력이 높은 브랜드를 집중적으로 육성한다는 구상이다. 아마존 글로벌셀링 코리아는 지난 27일 서울 강남구 그랜드 인터컨티넨탈 서울 파르나스에서 '아마존 뷰티 인 서울 2026'을 열고 내년도 K뷰티 지원 전략을 발표했다. 신화숙 아마존 글로벌셀링 코리아 대표는 신규 판매자의 초기 매출을 끌어올리는 '프로젝트 밀리언'과 선도 브랜드를 집중 지원하는 '프로젝트 타이탄'을 비롯해 헤어케어 시장 확대와 유럽 진출 지원을 위한 4대 프로젝트를 공개했다. 27일 서울 강남구 그랜드 인터컨티넨탈 서울 파르나스에서 열린 ‘아마존 뷰티 인 서울 2026’에서 신화숙 아마존 글로벌셀링 코리아 대표가 발언하고 있다./사진=박수림 기자 이번 전략에서 가장 강조한 것은 입점 이후의 실질적인 매출 성장이다. 신 대표는 "신규 셀러는 우리의 원동력이지만 단순히 제품을 출시하는 것만으로는 부족하다"고 짚었다. 신규 판매자의 아마존 입점이 꾸준히 늘고 있지만, 입점 첫해 얼마나 많은 매출을 올리느냐가 이후 사업의 지속 여부를 좌우한다는 설명이다. 이를 위해 추진하는 '프로젝트 밀리언'은 내년 신규 판매자 50개사가 미국 아마존에서 연 매출 100만 달러(약 13억 원)를 초과 달성하도록 돕는 것을 목표로 한다. 제품 기획부터 재고 관리, 광고 등 판매 전반에 걸쳐 맞춤형 지원을 제공한다. 이미 시장에 안착한 브랜드에 대해서는 지원 방식을 고도화한다. 아마존은 프로젝트 타이탄을 통해 성장 잠재력이 높은 선도 브랜드 7곳과 향후 3년간 협력하며 제품 출시부터 마케팅, 물류 운영까지 지원할 계획이다. 신 대표는 "선두 브랜드가 길을 열면 K뷰티 전체가 함께 성장한다"며 "이들 브랜드를 통해 검증된 성공 전략이 후발 K뷰티 기업들의 성장을 이끄는 밑거름이 될 것"이라고 강조했다. 아마존이 이처럼 전략을 고도화하는 배경에는 K뷰티의 폭발적인 성장세가 자리 잡고 있다. 올해 1~9월 한국 판매자의 아마존 뷰티 부문 매출은 전년 동기 대비 두 배 가까이 뛰었으며, 아마존 내 K뷰티의 성장 속도는 전체 뷰티 카테고리 평균보다 3배 이상 빠르다. 특히 미국에서 판매되는 K뷰티 제품의 약 44%가 아마존을 통해 거래되고 있다. K뷰티가 아마존의 핵심 성장 동력으로 자리 잡은 만큼 단순히 입점 브랜드 수를 늘리는 데 그치지 않고 개별 브랜드의 매출과 경쟁력을 키워 성장세를 이어가겠다는 판단이다. 신화숙 아마존 글로벌셀링 코리아 대표가 27일 서울 강남구 그랜드 인터컨티넨탈 서울 파르나스에서 진행된 ‘아마존 뷰티 인 서울 2026’에서 헤어케어에 대해 설명하고 있다./사진=박수림 기자 아마존은 스킨케어에 편중된 K뷰티 제품군 다변화에도 속도를 낸다. '프로젝트 실크로드'를 통해 내년 헤어케어와 웰니스 분야에서 신규 판매자 50곳을 유치하고 신제품 200종을 선보인다

items.t: Japan internet giant GMO says hackers posted stolen customer data
items.d: Japan's GMO Internet is verifying alleged customer data posted by suspected hackers following a cloud service breach.
items.fullText: Japanese internet company GMO Internet is investigating a data leak after suspected unauthorized access to its Onamae cloud desktop service, which provides virtualized desktops to financial traders. The IT and internet services giant said on its blog that it believes the attacker has published information allegedly linked to customers and its business. However, the contents are still being verified and the full extent of the incident remains unclear. GMO Internet has since advised customers to reset their passwords, amid receiving reports of “unauthorized operations” performed on customer trading accounts. The company said 27,000 servers may be affected by the breach. A spokesperson for GMO Internet did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment. The incident comes about a week after the Japanese firm’s cybersecurity unit separately reported finding evidence that a Chinese AI-enabled penetration testing tool called Artex had been used in hacks targeting companies across Japan. However, the company said it has not publicly established a connection between Artex and the breach of Onamae. The Artex tool was also used to hack financial institutions in South Korea in September, according to a report by CrowdStrike earlier this month. The attacks largely relied on exploiting weak security controls , such as a lack of multi-factor authentication. Artex’s Chinese developer has since stopped public updates and made the AI security tool closed-source after it was linked to cyberattacks targeting banks, per Reuters . A spokesperson at Japan’s Financial Service Agency (FSA) told TechCrunch that it issued guidance in May urging financial institutions to prepare for a rise in cybersecurity vulnerabilities. The regulator called for stronger basic defenses, including “vulnerability management, defense-in-depth and incident preparedness,” while encouraging firms to use AI and other security tools, the spokesperson added. items.t: General Compute raises $100 million Series A, countering the neocloud disaster narrative
items.d: General Compute is betting on inference chips from outside the Nvidia ecosystem.
items.fullText: CoreWeave, a publicly traded neocloud that rents out computing power for AI, has seen its stock price fall to a 12-month low, and Elon Musk is flexing $40 billion in debt for buying computing capacity and predicting that “200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation.” It’s not exactly the ideal week to announce a Series A for a neocloud. General Compute co-founder and CEO Finn Puklowski is unfazed. He’s bullish on CoreWeave’s chances, and thinks Musk is just talking his book to drive down the prices of the GPUs he wants to buy. Fears of a chip-led collapse are “massively overstated. I have people calling me up every single week asking me to do TPUs, GPUs, any chip, to get them more compute.” Just as important, he says, Anthropic’s bullish S-1 is “settling fears for today.” General Compute has found a niche building its cloud out of specialized inference chips built by Nvidia rivals. The company struck a $400 million deal to purchase new chips from SambaNova — the first debt financing of inference chips — and now has added Positron and Cerebras to its portfolio of chip suppliers. A deal with a large customer worth $100 million in annual recurring revenue has paved the way for the company to raise $100 million in Series A funding led by Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures. Valued at $60 million after a May seed round , General Compute is now worth $800 million post-money to its investors. The startup’s strategy is to zig where others zag. It focused on chips built for inference while everyone else chased GPUs. And instead of taking on a complex effort to build huge data centers, it uses smaller power sources, rents space in other companies’ data centers, and converts former bitcoin-mining sites into places that run AI models. items.fullText: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Announce General Availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Infrastructure Google Cloud A5X instances, accelerated by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, support European innovators with next-generation agentic and reinforcement learning infrastructure. October 21, 2026 by Uttara Kumar 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! General availability of the instances is coming next month, with planned expansion of availability to Europe — bringing an integrated platform for training, inference and large-scale reinforcement learning to cloud customers. A5X instances bring together NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, Google Cloud Virgo Network and Google Cloud’s fourth-generation advanced liquid-cooling technology for demanding agentic inference and reinforcement learning workloads at scale. Google Cloud plans to scale its Vera Rubin-based infrastructure to as many as 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multiple sites. Ineffable Intelligence , a London-based technology company founded by AlphaGo creator David Silver, was the first customer to access A5X. Ineffable is using the platform to advance large-scale reinforcement learning and shape “superlearner” systems that learn continuously from experience. October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence.
